section_summary: This section documents Allied decisions about allocating, retaining and scrapping former Japanese naval vessels after World War II. It includes vessel lists, a Soviet protest over the deferred division of 104 ships, a dispute over transferring vessels to the Korean Coast Guard, and a May 1948 scrapping report. Correspondence also addresses public access to Japanese and Italian ship allocations and the conversion of the Mikasa into an art museum.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of SWNCC papers to the Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards coordinating committee documents for information.
subfiles.summary: Encloses SWNCC papers and July 23 meeting minutes.

subfiles.title: Corrigendum to SWNCC 186/27
subfiles.about: Corrects the number of destroyer type vessels in a U.S. share paper.
subfiles.summary: The July 25 corrigendum changes two references from eight to nine destroyer type vessels.

subfiles.title: Conversion of the Mikasa into an art museum
subfiles.about: Forwards a press release announcing plans to convert the former flagship Mikasa.
subfiles.summary: The adviser hopes the conversion announcement will dispel concern that Japan is retaining a war memorial. The attached Navy Day release describes the museum plan and includes other occupation news.

subfiles.title: Disposition of ex-Japanese naval vessels: British ambassador
subfiles.about: Transmits a list of the disposition and status of remaining ex-Japanese naval vessels.
subfiles.summary: Refers to earlier correspondence and encloses the status list.

subfiles.title: Disposition of ex-Japanese naval vessels: Chinese ambassador
subfiles.about: Transmits a list of the disposition and status of remaining ex-Japanese naval vessels.
subfiles.summary: Refers to earlier correspondence and encloses the status list.

subfiles.title: Disposition of remaining ex-Japanese naval vessels
subfiles.about: Lists ship assignments and other dispositions by vessel type.
subfiles.summary: The list identifies destroyers, escorts, patrol craft, subchasers, minelayers, minesweepers, transports and auxiliaries assigned to four powers or retained for other uses. Its summary accounts for 239 vessels.

subfiles.title: Reply to A. J. McGinness on Japanese and Italian naval vessels
subfiles.from: John N. Allison, Department of State
subfiles.about: Provides the 1947 Japanese vessel drawing results and addresses Italian allocations.
subfiles.summary: Allison encloses a list of Japanese ships allocated in four drawings and says the Italian allocation list has not yet been published.

subfiles.title: Request for public information on naval vessel allocations
subfiles.about: Requests fuller information on Japanese and Italian ship divisions.
subfiles.summary: McGinness questions why allocations remain undisclosed and requests the names of ships assigned to each country.

subfiles.title: Disposition of ex-Japanese naval vessels: Soviet chargé d’affaires
subfiles.about: Transmits a status list of remaining ex-Japanese naval vessels.
subfiles.summary: Refers to the February 24 correspondence and encloses the vessel list.

subfiles.title: Disposition of remaining ex-Japanese naval vessels, copy
subfiles.about: Provides another copy of the 239-vessel disposition list.
subfiles.summary: The tables list individual ships by class and assignment or use, then total the vessels across the four powers, minesweeping, coast patrol, occupation service and other categories.

subfiles.title: Disposition of remaining ex-Japanese naval vessels, additional copy
subfiles.about: Provides an additional copy of the disposition list.
subfiles.summary: This copy again lists the ships by class, disposition and summary totals.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of SANACC 186/29 to Nanking
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge of the American Mission, Nanking
subfiles.about: Forwards a paper on the status of Japanese minor war vessels.
subfiles.summary: Transmits SANACC 186/29 following an earlier instruction on the U.S. share.

subfiles.title: Allocation of ex-Japanese naval vessels
subfiles.about: Sends copies of the four-power vessel allocation list.
subfiles.summary: Forwards two copies following a December 6 telephone conversation.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement form for despatch 1440
subfiles.about: Designates a replacement record copy of a Tokyo despatch.
subfiles.summary: The original action copy had not been returned for filing.

subfiles.title: Scrapping of ex-Japanese naval vessels
subfiles.about: Forwards a circular letter on scrapping former Japanese naval vessels.
subfiles.summary: Sends the November 29 circular addressed to Allied missions; summary reports were unavailable.

subfiles.title: Follow-up questions on destroyers and Italian vessels
subfiles.about: Questions missing Japanese destroyers and continued secrecy over Italian allocations.
subfiles.summary: McGinness asks about Harukaze, Kamikaze and other unallocated destroyers, and urges publication of Italian ship assignments.

subfiles.title: Suggested reply on Italian vessel allocations
subfiles.from: W. B. Sale, Division of European Affairs
subfiles.about: Explains why Italian naval vessel allocations have not been published.
subfiles.summary: Sale says the Council of Foreign Ministers agreed to withhold publication pending release by the Four Power Commission.

subfiles.title: Handwritten file notes
subfiles.about: Contains largely illegible handwritten notes apparently related to destroyer disposition.
subfiles.summary: The OCR does not support a reliable reading of the notes.

subfiles.title: Reply to McGinness on unallocated destroyers and Italian allocations
subfiles.about: Answers questions about Harukaze, Kamikaze and the unpublished Italian vessel list.
subfiles.summary: Bond says both destroyers will be sunk or scrapped and no further destroyer drawings are planned; the Italian list will be released later.

subfiles.title: Soviet protest over the remaining 104 Japanese warships
subfiles.about: Protests deferral of the four-power division of 104 former Japanese warships.
subfiles.summary: The Soviet government argues that delaying the remaining division violates the four-power agreement and requests immediate completion. Pages 41–42 provide the English translation; pages 43–45 contain the original Russian note.

subfiles.title: Request for facts concerning the Soviet protest
subfiles.from: J. K. Penfield, Department of State
subfiles.to: Colonel B. F. Taylor, Army General Staff
subfiles.about: Seeks information for a reply to the Soviet note.
subfiles.summary: Encloses a translation of the January 3 protest and requests the facts behind SCAP’s deferral.

subfiles.title: U.S. reply to Soviet protest on vessel division
subfiles.about: Explains the U.S. position on deferring the division of remaining Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: The note reviews the 1945 agreement, earlier vessel lists and division of 135 ships. It states that the remaining vessels are needed for occupation duties and that SCAP may defer their disposition until they become available.

subfiles.title: Copy of U.S. reply for the British ambassador
subfiles.about: Sends a copy of the U.S. reply to the Soviet protest.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the reply concerning former Japanese combatant vessels.

subfiles.title: Copy of U.S. reply to Soviet protest
subfiles.about: Repeats the U.S. explanation for deferring the remaining vessel division.
subfiles.summary: This copy states that 135 ships have been divided and that SCAP may retain remaining vessels while needed for occupation and surrender tasks.

subfiles.title: Remaining ex-Japanese naval vessels as of February 12, 1948
subfiles.from: Charles E. Saltzman, State–Army–Navy–Air Force Coordinating Committee
subfiles.about: Forwards SANACC 186/30 for information and possible action.
subfiles.summary: Transmits a copy of the vessel status paper.

subfiles.title: Handling of SANACC 186/30
subfiles.about: Recommends keeping the vessel status list in Department files.
subfiles.summary: Notes that SCAP supplied the list only to the U.S. Allied Council member.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of SANACC vessel papers to Nanking
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge of the American Mission, Nanking
subfiles.about: Forwards two papers on ex-Japanese naval vessel disposition.
subfiles.summary: Encloses SANACC 186/30 and 186/31.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of SANACC 186/31 to Tokyo
subfiles.to: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards the U.S. reply to the Soviet ambassador on vessel division.
subfiles.summary: Encloses SANACC 186/31 and identifies the January Soviet note it answers.

subfiles.title: Proposed permanent transfer of Japanese vessels to the Korean Coast Guard
subfiles.from: Ray S. Olaux, War Department Civil Affairs Division
subfiles.about: Requests concurrence on a proposed transfer of former Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: Forwards a draft message and SCAP letter with enclosures for review.

subfiles.title: Draft decision on Korean Coast Guard vessels
subfiles.about: Proposes permanently transferring eleven former Japanese vessels for Korean Coast Guard use.
subfiles.summary: Treats the vessels as surrendered enemy material outside the four-power division.

subfiles.title: SCAP letter on vessels for the Korean Coast Guard
subfiles.from: R. M. Levy for the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.to: Adjutant General, Department of the Army
subfiles.about: Explains the temporary loan of eleven Japanese vessels to Korea.
subfiles.summary: SCAP says permanent transfer lacks authority and asks how the Korean Coast Guard would replace the vessels if they must be returned.

subfiles.title: Recommendation for permanent transfer of Japanese vessels
subfiles.from: U.S. Army Military Government in Korea
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Requests permanent transfer of Japanese vessels to the Korean Coast Guard.
subfiles.summary: The military government describes coastal patrols, anti-smuggling work, navigational aid duties and repair constraints. It recommends transferring twelve Japanese vessels or equivalent replacements; the attached inventory records eleven Japanese tugs on loan.

subfiles.title: Japanese vessels on loan to the Korean Coast Guard
subfiles.from: U.S. Army Military Government in Korea
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Adds operational reasons for permanently retaining eleven Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: The letter says the vessels suit shallow harbors, patrols and navigation work, cost less to operate, and are easier to repair than American vessels. It requests permanent transfer before current advisers depart.

subfiles.title: State Department objection to the proposed Korean transfer
subfiles.about: Declines concurrence with the permanent transfer proposal.
subfiles.summary: Argues that omission from SCAP’s schedule does not remove the other powers’ claims under the Byrnes–Molotov agreement.

subfiles.title: Army request to reconsider Korean Coast Guard transfer
subfiles.from: G. P. Lynch, War Department Civil Affairs Division
subfiles.about: Urges reconsideration of the proposed vessel transfer to Korea.
subfiles.summary: Lynch argues the vessels are vital to Korean security and difficult to replace, and asks for an urgent answer to SCAP.

subfiles.title: Draft cable opposing transfer of former Japanese vessels
subfiles.about: States that authority to transfer the vessels to Korea is lacking.
subfiles.summary: The draft says the vessels remain subject to division among four powers.

subfiles.title: May 1948 report on destruction of ex-Japanese combatant vessels
subfiles.about: Transmits the Naval Forces Far East monthly scrapping report.
subfiles.summary: Reports cumulative destruction of 34 major ships, 40 submarines and 83 Koryus, and 117 minor ships.

subfiles.title: Destruction of ex-Japanese combatant vessels: May 1948
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Records May 1948 scrapping progress for former Japanese combatant vessels.
subfiles.summary: The report names vessels completed during May and adds Katsura to the scrapping program. Its tables track major ships, submarines and smaller vessels by tonnage and completion, then list completely scrapped ships, dates and yards. The enclosure continues beyond page 80 of this section.
